name: Zhi Gong
intro: I develop phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC) methods and software for electronic-structure calculations, with a focus on trial wave functions and overlap calculations.
blog_description: Notes on computational chemistry, scientific computing, and research methods.
about: I am a Ph.D. student in Chemistry at Rice University, advised by James Shee. My current research focuses on developing phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC) methods and code, with an emphasis on trial wave functions and overlap calculations. I work with restricted, unrestricted, and generalized Hartree-Fock references and full configuration interaction trial wave functions.

Before joining Rice, I studied Chemistry at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and was an exchange student at the University of California, Berkeley. In Martin Head-Gordon's group, I investigated the role of Criegee intermediates in unsaturated lipid autoxidation using electronic-structure calculations and reaction-path analysis. My earlier work with Jiang Gong explored waste-plastic upcycling, metal-organic frameworks, biodegradable foams, and porous carbon materials.

research.title: AFQMC method and code development
research.summary: Developing ph-AFQMC methods and code, with a focus on overlap calculations and trial wave functions.
details: My work in the Shee group includes code development for overlap calculations with restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF), unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF), generalized Hartree-Fock (GHF), and full configuration interaction (FCI) trial wave functions.

I also contribute to studies of trial-wave-function selection. A related publication examines the accuracy and limitations of UHF trial wave functions for ph-AFQMC calculations of three iron-sulfur clusters.

research.title: Criegee intermediates in lipid autoxidation
research.summary: Investigated the formation and consumption of Criegee intermediates in the autoxidation of unsaturated lipids through computational reaction-mechanism analysis.
details: In the Head-Gordon group, I used autodE to implement an initial mechanistic hypothesis and Q-Chem to perform geometry optimizations, vibrational-frequency analyses, and single-point energy calculations.

I investigated transition states using the freezing string method and transition-state optimization, then used intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations to examine reaction pathways. This work informed comparisons between the proposed mechanism and earlier studies.

research.title: Waste upcycling and functional materials
research.summary: Explored routes from waste polyester to metal-organic frameworks and porous carbon, alongside biodegradable foams for solar evaporation and energy conversion.
details: In Jiang Gong's group, I investigated the conversion of waste poly(ethylene terephthalate) into luminescent lanthanum metal-organic framework (La-MOF) nanoparticles. The project combined ball-milling synthesis, materials characterization, and density functional theory calculations to study Fe(III) sensing.

I also worked on biodegradable porous foams prepared by melt blending and surface coating for simultaneous solar evaporation and thermoelectricity generation. Related collaborations explored chromium metal-organic frameworks and porous carbon nanosheets derived from waste polyester.
